data.title: Ceramic glaze
data.content:
Composite body, painted, and glazed bottle. [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), 16th century ([Metropolitan Museum of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Museum_of_Art "Metropolitan Museum of Art"))

Detail of dripping rice-straw [ash glaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ash_glaze "Ash glaze") (top), Japan, 1852

**Ceramic glaze**, or simply **glaze**, is a [glassy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glass "Glass") coating on ceramics. It is used for decoration, to ensure the item is impermeable to liquids and to minimize the adherence of pollutants.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceramic_glaze#cite_note-Division-1)

Glazing renders [earthenware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthenware "Earthenware") impermeable to water, sealing the inherent [porosity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porosity "Porosity") of earthenware. It also gives a tougher surface. Glaze is also used on [stoneware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoneware "Stoneware") and [porcelain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcelain "Porcelain"). In addition to their functionality, glazes can form a variety of surface finishes, including degrees of glossy or matte finish and color. Glazes may also enhance the underlying design or texture either unmodified or inscribed, carved or painted.
